newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cuddly Koalas get the snip.
newsitem.headline: Cuddly Koalas get the snip.

text.p: Wildlife authorities on Monday began sterilising koalas, the cuddly Australian marsupial, to prevent their overcrowding on a sanctuary island after a public outcry killed off plans to have thousands culled.
Koala management coordinator Drew Laslett said the South Australian state government had decided against the koala cull on Kangaroo Island for political and economic reasons.
"It is recognised that images beamed around the world of koalas falling out of trees would not do our tourism much good at all," Laslett told Reuters.
Instead, officials plan to sterilise up to 3,000 of the animals, relocate hundreds to the mainland, and try to improve the island's habitat in a A$635,000 (US$495,000) programme.
Kangaroo Island, just off the South Australian coast, is home to a number of endangered species, among them the Tammar wallaby, brushtail possum, and sea lions.

Wildlife officials warned last year that the island's koalas, introduced in the 1920s amid fears they could become extinct on the mainland, now numbered about 5,000 and were threatening themselves and their habitat through overcrowding.

The koalas flourished on the island's eucalyptus trees, unrestrained by natural breeding checks like bushfires, dingoes or indigenous Aboriginal hunters. They have also been safe from the disease chlamydia which has struck many mainland koalas.
Officials said male koala vasectomies had already been used but it would be the first time that female koalas have to face sterilisation after tubal ligations trials at Adelaide zoo.
